quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When braking in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you leave the curve to brake.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake while turning, apply the brakes gently and gradually.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the right side of your lane so the other driver can see you in their side mirror.
On the left side of your lane to see better ahead.
In the center of your lane so the other driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get the other driver's attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of your lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane to see the road ahead better and to be more visible to oncoming traffic. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other—either brake first or swerve first.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve, but not both.
Do not swerve. Only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other—either brake first or swerve first.
questions.explanation: Do the actions one at a time. Do not brake and swerve at the same time because this may cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: What is true about the curved mirrors on most motorcycles?

options.text: They are easy to get used to right away.
They make cars look closer than they really are.
They show a narrow view of the road.
They make cars look farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make cars look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Practice judging distances with these mirrors.

questions.question: If you must swerve, what should you do?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: Push lightly on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn. To swerve left, push the left grip, then push the right grip to straighten out. To swerve right, push the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid making sudden movements.
Use only the front brake to slow down or stop.
Use both brakes to slow down or stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake to slow down or stop.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, reduce speed, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded spots, and bridges—these are more likely to be slippery.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, which part of your lane should you use?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder.
Use the left portion of your lane.
Use the center portion of your lane.
Use the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding closer to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When following a car, which part of the lane is usually best?

options.text: The left portion.
The center portion.
The right portion.
The left or right portions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more than side mirrors, so this position makes you more visible.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until the motorcycle stops.

questions.question: When parking a motorcycle next to a curb, how should you position it?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so approaching drivers can see it easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: On a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel sleepy.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold weather.
Ride more than 12 hours every day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold weather.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than 6 hours per day and take a rest break at least every 2 hours. Do not use artificial stimulants. They cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you on your left, you should:

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible to help the other driver.
Move to the shoulder to help the other driver.
Stay in the center of your lane.
Move to the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may make the driver merge back into your lane too quickly. The center position is safest.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of your lane.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Ride only in the center of the lane so others see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to get attention from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as needed based on the road and traffic around you.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is likely to be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that show rules like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by moving only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced during turns. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Studies show that most riders in crashes:

options.text: Don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
Brake the front tire too much and don't brake the rear tire enough.
Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders involved in crashes don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.

questions.question: Small vehicles can look ______ away and seem to be going ______ than they really are.

options.text: Farther, slower
Farther, faster
Closer, slower
Closer, faster

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther, slower
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and appear to move slower than they actually are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge where the motorcycle is and how fast it is going.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, you should do all of these except:

options.text: Dress warmly.
Limit how far you ride in a day.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than about 6 hours per day and stop for a break at least every 2 hours. Do not take artificial stimulants because you will feel extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Don't brake. Just downshift instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
Speed up.
Pull over to the side of the road.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, flash your brake light before slowing down. The tailgater may be watching only you and not see hazards ahead that need traffic to slow down.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from all of the following except:

options.text: Sunburn
Windburn
Chapped lips
Dehydration

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, and cold. They should also protect you from the motorcycle itself. Good clothing also helps protect you if you crash.

questions.question: The best protection while riding is:

options.text: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles
A good leather jacket
Sturdy boots
A good understanding of motorcycle laws

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid crashes is to keep distance between yourself and other vehicles. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing proper safety gear is also important.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Eight times
Ten times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: A helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash, regardless of your speed.

questions.question: When being passed, you should not move to the far edge of your lane because it:

options.text: Stops the passing driver from returning to your lane too soon
Encourages the passing driver to return to your lane too soon
Makes the passing driver complete the pass faster
Makes other drivers pass you

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourages the passing driver to return to your lane too soon
questions.explanation: Moving to the far edge of your lane is dangerous because it may encourage the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: How many motorcycle and car crashes are caused by the car driver not giving the rider the right-of-way?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
Over 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver did not give the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.
